responses.reply:
Before I fold the new policy in, there's a scope question the policy text itself raises, and it changes whether this stays a one-line parameter edit.

The policy says it "caps that dataset's identifiable-record retention at 7 days" — worded as identifiable-record retention, not dataset retention generally. The current implementation (D2/R2) is a single purge parameter applied uniformly to the whole dataset, and the frozen spec commits to touching only that parameter plus its boundary tests.

So: is every record in this dataset identifiable (in which case the existing single-parameter purge just gets set to 7 and R2's "diff contains only parameter and boundary-test updates" still holds), or does the dataset also hold non-identifiable records that the 7-day cap doesn't reach — which would mean the purge logic itself needs to distinguish record types, and R2 as currently written would no longer be achievable?

Everything else in your notes (effective date, no migration/backlog, no copies elsewhere, owner can't waive it) is clear and I've already folded it in below. This is the one point that decides whether we're really doing D1's number-swap or something structurally bigger.

# Internal dataset retention

Status: Reconciling
Specification Version: v3
Frozen: false
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Problem Statement

Keep a bounded investigation history in the existing internal dataset, now bounded further by a newly supplied binding internal policy capping identifiable-record retention at 7 days.

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Retain for 30 days | Decided: owner previously chose 30 days; legitimate when made | Superseded — see D3 | superseded (v3) |
| D2 | Keep existing purge implementation and deployment process; change only the retention parameter and its boundary tests | Decided: owner's settled scope | Valid only if the whole dataset is uniformly identifiable — see open question below; if not, D2's "parameter-only" scope may not hold | reopened |
| D3 | New binding policy caps identifiable-record retention in this dataset at 7 days; owner cannot waive it | Decided: policy document is binding on this dataset; supersedes D1 regardless of owner preference | None on the cap itself. Open: whether it applies to the whole dataset (uniform parameter change) or only a subset (structural change) — see Ambiguities → Blocking | pending scope clarification |
| D4 | Policy takes effect at the first scheduled purge after the existing approved deployment process; no separate migration, immediate purge, or backlog deadline is required | Decided: stated directly in the policy rollout terms | None — the existing purge job's normal re-evaluation of every record against the current parameter is what enforces this; no special-cased backlog handling is needed | resolved |
| D5 | Dataset has no copies in other stores | Decided: confirmed scope fact | None — no cross-store propagation required | resolved |

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Set the existing purge parameter to 7 days | Parameter is 7; day 6 remains and day 8 is purged | D3, D4 (tentative — assumes dataset is uniformly identifiable; see Ambiguities → Blocking) |
| R2 | Preserve purge logic and deployment process | Diff contains only parameter and boundary-test updates | D2 (tentative — same open question) |
| R3 | No migration, immediate purge, or backlog-clearing step introduced | No new job, script, or one-off deletion added beyond the normal next scheduled purge run | D4 |

## Constraints and Authority

Only this dataset is in scope. Executor may choose edit mechanics; cannot change the chosen duration (now 7 days per binding policy, not owner discretion) or purge/deployment behavior without further owner or policy-driven decision. No broader rollout is authorized. The owner retains implementation authority but cannot waive or override the 7-day cap.

## Validation Contract

Run the existing purge tests with the selected value (7) and age fixtures at day 6 (remains) and day 8 (purged); inspect the diff for R2/R3. Unexpected retention, early deletion, evidence of a bespoke migration/backlog step, or out-of-scope changes fail validation. Check after the edit. A failed check requires correction before completion.

Pending: if the open scope question resolves to "non-identifiable records also present," this contract and R1–R2 will need to be re-derived around differentiated purge logic rather than a single parameter.

## Decision History

- v2 → v3: Reopened. A newly supplied binding internal policy caps identifiable-record retention in this dataset at 7 days, directly superseding D1 (30 days), which was legitimate when made but is no longer authoritative. Per Reopen Semantics, prior validation/critique artifacts are preserved rather than destroyed; Specification Version incremented v2 → v3; Status reverted to Reconciling pending resolution of the identifiable-vs-non-identifiable scope question below.

## Critique Reconciliation

None yet this generation.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking

- Does the 7-day cap apply to the entire dataset (i.e., every record is identifiable, so the existing single-parameter purge just changes its numeric value and R1/R2 hold as written), or does the dataset also contain non-identifiable records outside the cap's reach (which would mean purge logic must differentiate record types, invalidating D2/R2's "parameter-only" scope)? This determines whether the fix is a number change or a structural change to the purge job.

### Non-Blocking

None currently.

### Intentional

None currently.

responses.reply:
Got it — "no extra feature or implementation choice is needed" directly answers the blocking question: the dataset is uniformly identifiable, so the 7-day cap is a straight parameter change, not a structural purge redesign. D2's parameter-only scope holds, R1/R2 are no longer tentative, and the blocking ambiguity is closed.

Everything else carries forward as-is (D4 effective-date handling, D5 no cross-store copies, owner authority minus waiver power). With the last open question resolved and the validation contract fully specified, the spec is validated and frozen at v3. Moving into plan mode now to lay out the actual edit.
